item.title: (SEEKING GREENLIGHTS) Hold on, why?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Typical SCP article including logs of every asked question, their host's reactions, and outcomes.

+Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook/Attention Grabber, and Notes
- why?

Elevator Pitch: The anomaly is an infohazard that induces a great sense of curiosity to individuals who have gained any information regarding it. Individuals with knowledge of the SCP initially ask themselves a certain question, regardless of which it is unknown to the individual or not, or classified or not. The subjects have no control over whatever question they ask. That is known as Stage 1 of the "infection". Stage 2 makes the individual have a great urge in research, usually that of the question they asked themselves. In certain individuals, Stage 3 may manifest. Stage 3 is death by insanity, believed to have been caused by the exponential growth of their will to find information or their "ultimate answer" to their questions. Stage 3 is only known to manifest if ever an individual asks themselves a certain impossibility, or possibly classified information. The infohazard is only lethal whenever an individual expires after 3 years of infection.

Central Narrative: The infohazard was detected after a lack of personnel morale. Plenty of personnel was observed asking "why" to themselves, with the situation growing large enough to be taken into consideration by the O5 council. Journals were distributed to affected personnel in an attempt to learn the nature of the phenomenon. The journals contain the questions, reactions, and outcomes of the personnel.

Examples:

Dr. █████

Q: Why did ███████ cheat on me?
R: Disappointed
O: Has found answer after interrogating Dr. ███████

Janitor ██████████

Q: How did O5-12 even get to █████████?
R: Confused
O: Janitor ██████████ was detained and taken into custody, interviewed. O5-12 then administered Class A amnestics

Dr. ███

Q: Why did Wondertainment make the █████████████ product line?
R: Extreme confusion
O: Subject was unable to recieve an answer, thus requesting amnestics.

Dr. ███████████

Q: How did SCP-█████ go to that other narrative?
R: Confused, striken with anxiety
O: Detained, interrogated by O5-██, was administered Class B amnestics. O5-██ claims it as a good way to determine possible future SCP's

Hook/Attention Grabber: A very dangerous or beneficial infohazard, causes great curiosity among the infected. Causes you to question anything, everything.

Additional notes: I'd prefer this article to be a great motivation when it comes to philosophical ideals, and the act of always questioning. But why?

item.title: Re: Possible Keter Class article Hurricane Omega
item.content:encoded:
"In the event that more than twenty-one named tropical cyclones occur in the Atlantic basin in a season, additional storms will take names from the Greek alphabet."

24 letters in the Greek alphabet, so that's 21+24 which is 45. 45 tropical cyclones/hurricanes in one hurricane season. That's immensely unrealistic unless it's an XK-Class end-of-the-world scenario.

That's the idea, it is an XK-Class EotW Scenario. But the record itself is what is anomlious.

So.. this seems like a tale to me. Not an SCP object. It's just a hurricane. They die out after a few weeks or less. An SCP causes a hurricane, the Foundation tries to stop it. That should be a tale. Also, how do you contain a hurricane?

Well, I had the idea that the story was found in several glass bottles that look to have been in the ocean for decades, but one is found in the Arizona Desert, one in the Himalayas, One in the Alps, and so on and so on. Basically, they are all found far from any body of water. The information in the bottles tells the story of a Hurricane season so devastating that when Hurricane Omega hits it does not die out, much like the red spot on Jupiter. The fact these bottles are found with the info in them makes no sense because no such event has happened yet, and no one can tell if maybe SCP-2000 activated and fixed the damage or if the bottles came from somewhere else.

And you don't contain a hurricane, you neutralize it.

Overall, this idea is interesting but as an SCP it would not work (it's not anomalous). If you can make it out as a tale, that would hopefully work out and be interesting. Also, its never specified if it's a tale or an SCP.

Well, the Storm itself could be anomalous as an XK event that maybe the Chaos Insurgency set off and lost control. I am thinking the Foundation built a Special site called the ARK just for such an emergency. I am thinking of making it a tale like the one that goes along with SCP-5000. That is kind of where I got the idea.

item.title: Moderator Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Triple-bracket links are superior to single-bracket links and should be used where possible, such as cross-links with other pages on the wiki. As such they are considered allowable formatting edits on pages.

However, it is important to be sure that they are used appropriately. Triple-bracket links with a full URL (e.g. [[[http://www.scpwiki.com/some-page]]]) are no better than single-bracket links, and some kinds of references (most notably forums) cannot be referenced using triple-bracket page name notation (i.e. [[[some-page|Link label here]]].

Provided that you are only editing pages you come across casually, I'm fine with these changes. Please do not seek out large numbers of pages to edit. If you have an extensive list of pages to be changed, please bring it to staff instead.

Also note that staff reserves the right to issue cease-and-desist orders for any edits being carried out in an improper manner.

item.title: Question re: Editing others' articles
item.content:encoded:
Hi, I hope I've found the right place for site rules questions. My question's about this rule (emphasis mine):

Editing others' articles: You may correct grammar, spelling, or formatting errors on other peoples' articles. Please put a summary of changes in the 'description of changes' box. Any further edits require permission from the original author or Rewrite team.

Often, an on-site link (triple brackets) is formatted as an external link (single brackets). As the Google Chrome users among you may already know, these external links don't work for some users while they are logged in (because we visit scp-wiki.wikidot.com instead of scpwiki.com as a login workaround; visiting any link formatted as https://scpwiki.com/whatever gives us an error message1). Clicking a link that ought to be an on-site link and receiving an error is unpleasant, as is manually replacing scpwiki with scp-wiki.wikidot in the address bar.

I don't know if using the 'wrong' link type is technically a formatting error, but I am hoping to receive mod/admin confirmation that it falls under this category.2 Changing these links' format type would not alter the article text, it would just make the links work properly for those of us who have to use scp-wiki.wikidot.com instead of scpwiki.com for technical reasons.

Getting author permission each and every time, just to change link formatting type from external to on-site, would be hugely annoying for both the editor and the author. I am hoping that we readers can be allowed to make these formatting changes without obtaining author permission each time.

So, tl;dr: If a link is formatted as an external link, but would work properly as an on-site link, may we go ahead and make that formatting change without bothering the author for their permission?

Footnotes
1. Note that the error only appears when an external link specifies https. It's some sort of certificate recognition error. Links formatted as on-site links work fine for us Chrome users, because wikidot helpfully inserts whichever base address the reader is already using.
2. I actually created an account because I wanted to fix various minor errors as I came across them while reading.

item.title: Re: Drooling Path 3
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
[-] Close

The Conrad aspects of this feel…weird. For a story about Conrad going on a journey to the Atherton Hotel, it very much feels like the actual journey is secondary and all of the story is just kinda covering him thinking about how he feels about the journey as a whole and planning out various aspects of it. This isn’t necessarily bad per se but it makes it feel insubstantial on it’s own since there’s not really a lot happening; and it also feels like it’s a poor setup to a fourth part of this since we don’t really get a feel for what will happen at the Hotel. Specifically: whilst Conrad dwells on the maybes a lot, the lack of knowledge (or even plausible theories) for what he might find at the Hotel means that his arrival there doesn’t inspire emotions within me. I’m not worried Conrad will die, or excited for the revelation he’ll find or really much of anything because I genuinely have no idea what he’ll find there. And so without there being much interesting happening on his journey either, it feels…underwhelming.

The James aspects have similar issues: setting up that James might end up in danger and his increasing investigations into the CD he stole is cool but it doesn’t get time to go anywhere. He never listens to the CD, and so it just feels like this whole section is a holding pattern as we wait for something to happen.

I think on it’s own either one of these stories feeling very interstitial like this, like this is a quiet break before the cool action, could work; but neither feeling like they advance this in an interesting way leads to this piece just feeling…too much like it’s padding out the story more. I wouldn’t think this was as much of an issue if the first parts in the story had been more exciting but since this brings the series up to ~9.5k words as a whole, I’m left feeling…drained and not really looking forward to the continuation a tonne?

I guess if I was to summarise, it’d be that it feels like this needs to setup the stakes more: some indication of how bad can the events go; not just in a vague ‘Conrad presumes he could die’ way but in a precise way where we can see the shape of the danger at least somewhat. Perhaps the best way to do this would be the addition of a third perspective, this time from either a neutral or antagonistic force, perhaps a narrator hinting at what awaits in the Atherton hotel, or perhaps a view from like, the hotel owner preparing some devious trap?

[-] Close

item.title: The Though Farmer
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight
SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a humanoid SCP whose main objective appears to be the collection of, what will be labeled for ease of understanding, thought energy. The exact nature of this energy is unknown, however it is known that SCP-XXXX is able to use this energy to influence or cause events. SCP-XXXX typically gains this energy by gathering followers for cults or religions it leads or influences, however other methods have been recorded.

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX begins its indoctrination process by introducing a cult it is involved with to it's target. SCP-XXXX then regularly manipulates it's target's focus to its cult via things the target enjoys. It is at this stage that the target decides to walk away, or become involved and proceed to the next stage. Eventually the target proceeds to the last stage. In this stage, the target becomes more engaged in cult activities which consumes a significant amount of the target's time. The target also sacrifices all 'optional' activities to make time for cult activities but still takes part in necessary daily activities, such as work, hygiene and eating. During this stage the target also has decreased cognitive functions. There is currently no known way to exit this stage, barring termination of the subject.

SCP-XXXX itself is a non-corporeal entity that is capable of appearing as almost any animal or person. SCP-XXXX is capable of appearing in the 'real' world as well as in the dreams of individuals. There has been no recorded physical interaction with SCP-XXXX, and it's incapable of moving objects. SCP-XXXX has also rarely interacted with foundation personnel.
SCP-XXXX current motives are unknown, however there are some conversations between foundation staff and SCP-XXXX that are in it's file.

Central Narrative: This SCP article focuses on SCP-XXXX's activities, what religions and cults SCP-XXXX has interfered with in history (that the foundation can find) SCP-XXXX's current endeavours, it's motives and communication with the foundation and, ultimately what it will do with its power (besides get more).

Hook: The hook (ATM) is the process that SCP-XXXX 'gains' additional people, as well as its interactions with the foundation and its end goal with what it wants to accomplish (Which will be a mystery, to maintain intrigue.).

Notes: While the whole emphasis on SCP-XXXX's motives and goals seems lacking in this post, I'll include some interactions with foundation personnel that will go more in depth.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: The Though Farmer

Yes, things that have been done before could be made to work, but only with a unique twist.

I would suggest you read a lot more articles to see what sorts of things work on the site nowadays, as opposed to what worked on the site back in its origins.

item.title: Re: LLUN Man Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
you're going about it wrong. If you want to keep the article mysterious, that makes sense. It does not make sense to keep the idea post mysterious.

The purpose of the greenlighting process is to convince at least two authors that you can communicate your idea in a compelling manner.

So… I am not concerned that you would not explain the aura in the idea post, I am concerned that it seems to have no connection to the anomalies as presented. I feel like you missed the point of my critique.

I think you need to sit down and simplify, make a cohesive anomaly about the one man and focus on his anomalous aspects that thematically connect to each other.

When I said this ^ it was not to suggest anything but that your idea felt too disjointed and you should simplify the core anomaly to make more cohesive sense.

You need to develop a cohesive proposal for the idea to communicate what your story is about.

No one is going to greenlight your concept without you explaining the concept. If you choose to withold and say something like "you'll learn about it in the article" I wouldn't trust that this will turn into an article that could survive.

item.title: Tale: Rabbit Seed-bombs
item.content:encoded:
A deprecated house is over run by an anomalous, self-perpetuating, rabbit warren and their poo. Their previous owners still occupy the house.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: Tale

Genre (Optional): Dark Comedy

Elevator Pitch: Two Foundation agents are sent to investigate a house overrun by rabbits in the Midwest. The house is found to have its own microclimate similar to the Pacific Northwest, and its ecosystem is self-perpetuating due to the anomalous rabbits. The previous owners are turned into rabbit people by parasitic baby rabbits.

Central Narrative: It’s revealed through the found documents, an owner’s journals, that they had two rabbits. Before they could get them spade and neutered, the vets office closed due to quarantine. Unable to be contained, going so far as to teleport, the male rabbits kept escaping and creating more litters. The owners hired the city compost to take their quickly escalating piles of rabbit poo.

+ show block
– hide block

Over time, firs, ferns, blackberries, and other Pacific Northwest foliage grows out of the rabbit poo at an expedited rate. The owners, and housemates, slowly turn into rabbit-people when parasitic baby rabbits burrow into the base of their skulls. (Similar to the Goa’uld from Stargate).

Two Foundation agents are sent to investigate the house and they traverse room to room to figure out the ill fate of the owners. They are chased out of the house by angry rabbits, and rabbit-people.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A deprecated house is over run by an anomalous, self-perpetuating, rabbit warren and their poo. Their previous owners still occupy the house.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts and properly space your paragraphs. ~Zyn

item.title: A teleporting bridge
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Other (Mystery/Curiosity)

Elevator Pitch: It's a teleporting bridge. It teleports whenever liquids or loose solids touch it, to a random waterway location. Containing it requires some experimentation and ingenuity, resulting in odd containment procedures that induce curiosity in readers who don't know what the anomaly is yet.

Central Narrative: The exacting, atypical containment procedures will lead the reader to wonder what anomaly is being contained. The description will answer that question, while prompting the reader to wonder why the containment procedures are so elaborate. The experiment log clarifies how researchers determined that simpler containment procedures were ineffective/insufficient.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The containment procedures involve the creation of an artificial miniature river ecosystem. Readers' expectations/hypotheses about the contained anomaly will be continually challenged or subverted by additional information in the containment procedure.

Additional Notes: This is my first SCP.

item.title: Re: (Awaiting greenlights) The elite soldier.
item.content:encoded:
Hey author, just pitching in my 2 cents.

This is really out of character for Anderson Robotics. Though this is not the first time they make an exoskeleton, it's certainly the first time they would be making a weapon of war! They're mostly known for making consumer grade products and fancy gizmos for the wealthy. A fighting exoskeleton that commits war crimes is definitely not something they would do. But that isn't to say Anderson Robotics isn't a moral bastion. Vincent Anderson, the founder, is known for being a cheat and a bit of a ruffian. There's also the fact that most AR products are powered by souls, which can lead to ethical questions.

Then there's the issue of the idea. Like zyn said, it's very typical of exoskeleton tropes and doesn't have much of interest going on for it.

item.title: Re: Television POV(Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the critique. After several days of brainstorming I came up with the idea of a researcher obsessed with finding his own point of view. He'd try to use d-classes to flip the channels for him. Once that proves to be ineffective as they'd only be able to get a couple million in a year, he opts to find ways to dampen the signal, he'd find out that a lead-lined room works and it decreases the range considerably to around 40 kilometers. After that he discovers a d-class pov, he'd get the d-class to stare into the tv. The d-class does and enters into the trance. The researcher shuts off the tv and after five minutes the d-class comes to, but the d-class can't remember anything, much to the researcher's frustration. Several days later, the d-class kills himself.

This piques the researcher's interest even more. "what did he see that compelled him to commit suicide?" So, much to the dismay of the other researchers, he finds his own pov.

The ending is from another researcher who writes that the first researcher looked very unaware of his surroundings, suffered terrible disassociation and ultimately killed himself. Concludes that any researcher who wishes to test the SCP must do under supervision from another researcher.

item.title: Re: Unforgettable
item.content:encoded:
► my detailed thoughts◄
- close

The Addendum will have a journal where the main story takes place.

Be careful of doing a journal for the vast majority of the story… you can lose the reader this way, I’d suggest focusing on multiple types of addendums.

When his anomaly manifested, however, he began to draw away from his friends and family, out of fear that they would remember him in a bad way.

How is this anomaly discovered? As being memorable could easily never come to the attention of the Foundation.

That is, until his anomaly manifested. It's not known exactly when it happened, but he noticed how people began to act off around him. This "offness" became more intense over time, until people started to reference things he did that he had trouble remembering, leading him to realise that he was unable to be forgotten.

I’m sorry, I don’t know that such a leap is believable. People can remember things about yourself that you’ve forgotten very easily… it’s happened to me multiple times. I don’t think this fits as a realization moment. Need something a bit more dramatic to make the kid realize he can’t be forgotten.

He drew away from everyone he knew, drawing the attention of the Foundation as a consequence.

There are tremendous amounts of people who aren’t social and isolate, why would this draw the Foundation’s attention?

Overall:

  • I’m not super interested in this anomaly, as its so subtle I am not sure what would lead the Foundation would even discover it, let alone find it worrying enough to contain. For example, I don’t think knowing this person, and remembering a lot about them, would even necessarily be noticed or threaten normalcy… as I don’t know that people would realize it is something unnatural.
  • I am a little lost as to the core narrative here, what is the point of this story? Other than this kid becoming socially isolated due to his anomaly (which I am not entirely convinced would be a reaction to this specific anomaly) I am not seeing much in the way of an arc. I think you could make it interesting, but that would require a personal grounded description of this kid’s experiences. I think that’s something you should focus on if you’re going to continue with this.
  • ultimately I think you should consider tweaking the anomaly, making it a little less subtle… something that would make the person withdraw from the society, and even if you keep this anomaly, you’ve got to tweak the discovery as currently its not really explained how the Foundation would even notice it.
